mainEntity.name: What is the best photo editing software for 2027?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a desktop library and RAW workflow, my starting recommendation is Lightroom Classic. Lightroom suits editing across devices; Capture One suits studio work; Affinity and Photoshop suit detailed image editing. The best choice depends on the work you need to do.

mainEntity.name: Are Lightroom and Lightroom Classic the same?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. They share many editing capabilities, but they are separate applications. Classic centres on a desktop catalogue and files on your drives. Lightroom offers cloud access across desktop, mobile and web, with local file editing also available on desktop.

mainEntity.name: Can I edit RAW files without a subscription?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Options include DxO PhotoLab, ON1 Photo RAW and Capture One's perpetual desktop licence. Affinity's core app is free. Check camera compatibility, edition differences and whether major upgrades cost extra.

mainEntity.name: Is Affinity Photo still a paid app?

acceptedAnswer.text: The current unified Affinity app includes free core photo editing tools with a Canva account. Older Affinity Photo licences belong to an earlier product offering. Premium Canva AI features in the current app require a qualifying paid plan.

mainEntity.name: Is Luminar a replacement for Lightroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be an alternative main editor if its RAW and creative tools meet your needs. Photographers who rely heavily on keywording, cataloguing and a large desktop archive should compare its library tools carefully with Lightroom Classic.

mainEntity.name: Do I need Photoshop as well as Lightroom?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not for every photograph. Lightroom can handle much everyday RAW development and selective editing. Photoshop is useful when you need detailed retouching, complex selections or compositing that goes beyond that workflow.

mainEntity.name: Should I buy a separate noise reduction app?

acceptedAnswer.text: Test the noise reduction in your main editor first. A specialist tool such as Topaz Photo may help with particular files, but compare results on your own images before adding another subscription.
